   Joann rode her bike at an average speed of 12 miles per hour for 3.5 hours. To find the distance she traveled, we use the formula:
   \[
   \text{Distance} = \text{Speed} \times \text{Time}
   \]
   Substituting the given values, we get:
   \[
   \text{Distance} = 12 \times 3.5 = 42 \text{ miles}
   \]
